note: Adapted from the original description of Hagen (1858), which consists of a Latin diagnosis and a detailed German description; only the alate is described, no soldier or worker (the author notes that he saw only dried male and female adults). Measurements keep the original unit, mm. The OCR used has a few misread letters (for example Rostroth=rostroth, Dornen and the like), which did not affect the reading of the characters; missing parts were not supplied with invented words.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Entirely rusty red, paler beneath, the mouthparts tinged dark brown; wings hyaline and smoky, the costa rusty red. Head medium-sized, flattened, smooth, oval, widest immediately behind the compound eyes; compound eyes small, slightly projecting, oval, placed far forward; occiput large, expanded, round; frons distinctly narrowed, its anterior corners nearly right-angled and oblique, with two small pits on each side and one larger pit between the eyes; ocelli entirely absent. Antennae slightly longer than the head and pronotum together, slender, 27-segmented: segment 1 thicker than the rest, about twice as long as wide, cylindrical; segment 2 as long as wide; segment 3 shorter; the following few segments smaller, more or less approximated, spherical; the segments after these larger and spherical; the terminal segment elongate, slender, oval. Labrum square with rounded corners, slightly overhanging the black mandibles. Pronotum distinctly narrower than the head, flat, smooth, about twice as wide as long; anterior margin concave in a shallow arc, the anterior corners right-angled and rounded, the sides straight, passing behind into a semicircular posterior margin; the mid-longitudinal suture hardly visible, with a pit on each side of it reaching the margin. Abdomen short oval; abdominal appendages long and stout, conical, 5-segmented, the basal 4 segments short and ring-like, the terminal segment long oval. Wings large and broad, about twice as long as the body; anterior margin nearly straight, the apex obliquely truncate, the posterior margin rounded; costal cell broad, widening towards the apex, with 10 oblique veins. Measurements: length with wings 26 mm; body length 11 mm; wing span 46 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The author saw only dried male and female specimens, no soldier and no worker. Locality California (about Ross's settlement near San Francisco), Museum of St Petersburg; collected by Walker from the Hardwicke collection (British Museum); Louisiana, collected in 1851 by Ida Pfeiffer (Vienna Museum). The author points out that this species is the closest relative among the amber termites and was the only living species of the genus Termopsis at the time, and considers that Walker's T. castaneus should be placed in this species. It was published under the genus name Termopsis and is now placed in Zootermopsis.
